od_023_position: OD-023 is PENDING. Current Status: 'Pending owner approval'. Its exact question is which issuing authority, permission, entropy and wire format, TTL and equality boundary, one-use consumption point, binding tuple, retry/replay behavior, and new-material reference transport define the 'fresh rotation token' that `integration-interim-v1` requires to rotate a Credential. Blocking Impact records: Volume II -- no, because the path is absent rather than ambiguous and `UPSTREAM-V1-CREDENTIAL-ROTATION-TOKEN-009` correctly refuses to resolve it; implementation -- no under the fail-closed interim and prelaunch operation with synthetic secrets; production -- storing a real Mailgun provider secret is blocked because SEC-REQ-016 requires a defined per-credential-class rotation and maximum age policy the interim does not supply; feature -- every rotation behaviour and any contractual secret-rotation claim are blocked until approval. The register maps OD-023 to CAP-021/WF-014 because that is where the Mailgun Integration's Credential is USED, not because WF-014 owns rotation. The withheld limb is therefore exactly credential rotation BEGIN and COMPLETE. PERMITTED and contracted in full here: representing a Credential with its frozen `pending`/`active`/`rotating`/`revoked`/`expired` state set and its conceptual pending-material pointer; every unaffected credential usage, meaning delivering notifications against an already-active unexpired Credential at the platform-managed provider checkpoint; the read-only Credential and material version identifiers that WF-014's Audit and Observability clause expressly requires; and the terminal mapping of an unavailable, invalid, revoked or expired Credential, which `integration-interim-v1` and `notification-policy-v1` both define independently of rotation. PROHIBITED and isolated: rotation initiation, rotation completion, any token semantics that pre-empt the decision, and any route, command, job or event performing the withheld behaviour. Concretely, under `credential-rotation-blocked-interim-v1`: no token issuer, permission, operation, route, wire format or TTL exists, so every mint request is denied as an undefined permission under the Permission Baseline; `BeginCredentialRotation` remains registered but unreachable and `CompleteCredentialRotation` has no independent entry; no path sets pending material, enters `rotating`, or accepts replacement material; no `CredentialRotationStarted` or `CredentialRotated` emission, outbox or Notification route, `credential_rotation_retry` scheduled action, or rotation DDL function or grant exists. Note that `credential.rotate` IS a canonical Permission Baseline token (protected explicit grant plus Support Session for SecurityOperator; credential lifecycle service executes accepted transition only). It is not invented and is not deleted here. It is simply unreachable, because OD-023 withholds the fresh rotation token that `integration-interim-v1` makes mandatory to begin rotation, and deny-by-default forbids inferring the token's issuer, format, lifetime, consumption point, binding or transport. od_032_position: OD-032 is PENDING and is cited by MTX-021 only. Notification and Delivery both appear in DM-REQ-001's omission list, so no canonical identifier namespace or lifecycle owner is assigned to either. Safe Interim Behavior: no record is added to DM-REQ-001, no namespace or lifecycle owner is inferred for an unassigned record, and no implementation may invent either; Volume I's existing logical field names and behavioural contracts for these records are unchanged and remain authoritative for behaviour; any Volume II or persistence artifact that requires a canonical namespace for an unassigned record remains blocked rather than choosing one. no_exactly_once_position: Mailgun supplies no provider-side idempotency. Volume I states it directly: the application deduplication key and the Mailgun user-variable correlation token 'are evidence lookup and local deduplication mechanisms only; they are not provider-side idempotency and cannot guarantee one external delivery', and 'External delivery may be zero, one, or more than one; F1 MUST NOT claim exactly-once delivery.' This contract therefore separates two distinct guarantees and never conflates them. The APPLICATION guarantee is exact and is asserted: exactly one claimed attempt receives exactly one first submission, and no executor re-enters an attempt at or after `submission_started`. The PROVIDER guarantee is absent and its absence is contracted: acceptance that cannot be disproved becomes `acceptance_unknown`, which is neither success nor terminal failure and has no age-based inference; a recipient-visible duplicate after acknowledged replay or provider behaviour is permitted and is not a specification failure. Duplicate tolerance is carried by the product action rather than by the transport: templates retain one logical action reference whose invitation, expiry, authorization, command replay and underlying product-transition rules remain independently idempotent, so receiving or using a duplicate email cannot duplicate authority or a product action.
telemetry_versus_domain_events_position: Volume I's WF-014 Domain Events line is a closed list of seventeen notification events plus the applicable `integration-interim-v1` Integration/Credential events. Everything else this slice observes is technical telemetry and MUST NOT be emitted as a domain event: authenticated Mailgun webhook ingress, provider event IDs, provider status text, transport certainty, the `delivery` queue depth, the provider concurrency gate, worker leases, adapter timing and end-to-end latency. The distinction is load-bearing here because the provider transport is unusually visible: a Mailgun `delivered` webhook is provider transport semantics, whereas `NotificationDelivered` is the product outcome the platform derives from it under the fixed reduction precedence. The two are never emitted as the same thing and a provider event never becomes a domain event by passthrough.

MTX-039.interface_type: Event-driven dispatch plus three application commands. The dispatch path is asynchronous: a routed logical event is consumed from the durable outbox, one logical Notification and its Deliveries are created, each Delivery attempt executes under a claimed lease, and uncertainty starts read-only reconciliation. The commands are Notification Policy activation, privileged replay, and the acting principal's own inbox read. Provider event ingress is an authenticated inbound transport surface, not a product command.
MTX-039.route: Not applicable - Volume I defines the commands, their permissions and their envelopes but no HTTP path, method or transport. Transport exposure is owned by API_CONTRACTS.md at the Volume II baseline. This holds for the inbox read too: OD-020 ratifies `notification.inbox.read` scoped to the acting principal's own inbox and binds it to WF-014, but a permission is not a route and Volume I fixes no path, method, pagination or projection for it. The authenticated Mailgun webhook ingress is a provider transport surface rather than a product route: Volume I fixes its authentication obligations - signature and timestamp authentication, resolution exclusively from an authenticated restricted locator carrying the correlation digest, claimed Delivery and replay generation - but names no path or method, it carries no product authorization, and failed signature or timestamp authentication is retained as restricted security telemetry and changes no state.
MTX-039.request_schema: Event consumption: the Logical Event Envelope plus a complete `notification_context_v1` carrying Organization ID; nullable Project ID; affected resource type/ID; initiating Account ID nullable for service work; initiating service identity nullable for human work; current status; reason code; action-reference type/ID; data classification; and the exact policy/definition versions governing visibility and outcome, with exactly one initiator form nonnull, plus the exhaustive trigger-specific required fields for its trigger class. Policy activation: expected active version, complete normalized route/template/selector content, `activation_mode=immediate`, and no client-supplied effective or expiry time. Replay: replay mode (`delivery_replay` or `empty_recipient_replay`), the source Delivery ID for `delivery_replay` or the source Notification ID for `empty_recipient_replay`, a 20-2,000 character reason, and `duplicate_delivery_risk_acknowledged` required true only when the source Delivery is `acceptance_unknown`.
MTX-039.response_schema: Event consumption returns one logical Notification carrying notification ID, triggering event ID and type, Organization and resource scope, template and policy versions, severity, action reference, occurred time, correlation ID, replay generation and aggregate status, with its immutable stored recipient snapshot and per-channel Deliveries. Policy activation returns the new immutable activated version with its commit-time effectiveness. Replay returns the linked new Notification generation and its single new Delivery for `delivery_replay`, or the newly resolved union's Deliveries for `empty_recipient_replay`, leaving every source record unchanged.
MTX-039.controller: Not applicable - no HTTP adapter is defined by Volume I; see route.
MTX-039.command: `Workflows::Wf014::ConsumeNotificationEvent` (executes `notification_route_v1` from the claimed outbox route and owns the resulting Notification/Delivery writes), `Workflows::Wf014::ExecuteDeliveryAttempt` (worker path, claims the attempt and performs at most one provider submission), `Workflows::Wf014::ReconcileDelivery` (worker path, read-only), `Workflows::Wf014::ConsumeProviderEvent` (authenticated ingress), `Workflows::Wf014::ActivateNotificationPolicy`, `Workflows::Wf014::RequestNotificationReplay`, `Workflows::Wf014::ReadOwnInbox` (nonmutating). WITHHELD under OD-023: `BeginCredentialRotation` remains registered but unreachable and `CompleteCredentialRotation` has no independent entry; neither is invoked from any path here.
MTX-039.command_input: As request_schema. The attempt claim input is the exact tuple `(delivery_id, replay_generation, attempt_number, request_digest)`. Resolved adapter-policy artifact ID/version/content hash and Integration/Credential/material versions are NOT inputs at claim: they are null at claim and are filled monotonically as prepared-stage validation resolves them.
MTX-039.command_output: One logical Notification per `(event_id, policy_version, template_version, generation)`; one stored deduplicated recipient snapshot; one Delivery per `(notification_id, recipient_id, channel, replay_generation)`; one claimed attempt per `(delivery_id, generation, attempt_number)`; one reconciliation per `(delivery_id, generation, sequence)` with sequence in 0/1/2/3; and exactly one escalation per `(delivery_id, generation, kind)` or, for an empty selector union, per `(notification_id, generation, kind)`.
MTX-039.actor: The Notification service identity dispatches and may invoke only the exact platform-managed integration checkpoint. Policy activation is an OrganizationAdmin holding `policy.notification.manage` for optional informational routes, templates and preferences only, or a SecurityOperator holding the same permission for security templates, support-queue roster and critical selectors only. Replay is a SecurityOperator in an approved time-bounded support session holding `notification.replay`. The inbox read is the acting principal reading only their own inbox. Owner-approval release and Integration/Credential lifecycle services hold only their named service permissions and are not reachable from the dispatch path.
MTX-039.organization_scope: The event Organization, taken from `notification_context_v1` and equal to the routed event's Organization; a `notification_context_v1` whose Organization or resource is inconsistent with the event fails consumption as `notification_event_invalid`. Selector components resolve active Accounts in the event Organization and resource scope only. A SecurityOperator support-queue component additionally requires an active roster entry in the Notification Policy.
MTX-039.aggregate: Notification as the logical root with its immutable recipient snapshot; Delivery as the per-recipient-per-channel root; DeliveryAttempt and DeliveryReconciliation as immutable checkpoint records under the Delivery; NotificationPolicy as an immutable versioned Policy Artifact; the escalation and the replay acknowledgement as immutable decision records. Integration and Credential are separate roots owned by `integration-interim-v1` and are read and validated at the checkpoint, never mutated by a Delivery.
MTX-039.aggregate_boundary: Event consumption commits Notification, its recipient snapshot and all its Deliveries in one transaction, because the route table, selector union and per-channel Delivery set are all derived from one event consumption and a partially created Notification would let a Delivery exist with no aggregate to recompute. The attempt claim is a separate transaction on the Delivery root and MUST precede Integration/Credential validation - that ordering is the whole point of the claim and is not an implementation preference. Each attempt result, each reconciliation result and each aggregate recomputation commits separately. Escalation is its own immutable decision record so that a failed escalation write can never silently vanish into a Delivery update. This is a bounded multi-root specialisation of the EM-III-011 default, required by WF-014 rather than chosen.
MTX-039.value_objects: NotificationState, DeliveryState, DispatchCheckpoint (`prepared`, `submission_started`, `recorded`), Severity (`informational`, `warning`, `critical`), ReplayGeneration, AttemptNumber, RequestDigest, ApplicationDeduplicationKeyDigest, ProviderCorrelationTokenDigest, AdapterPolicyIdentity fixed to `mailgun-email-v1`, AdapterCodeVersion, IntegrationVersion, CredentialVersion, MaterialVersion, ProviderMessageId, ProviderEventId, TransportCertainty, RetryClassification, ReconciliationSequence (0, 1, 2, 3), ReconciliationOutcome (`matched`, `none`, `ambiguous`, `dependency_error`, `authentication_failed`), ReplayMode (`delivery_replay`, `empty_recipient_replay`), ClassificationCeiling, ReasonCode, NotificationContextV1. WITHHELD under OD-032: no canonical identifier namespace is asserted for Notification or Delivery.
MTX-039.domain_service: Not applicable - WF-014 names no domain service. The selector union, the provider status mapping, the authenticated-event mapping, the `terminal_failed > delivered > accepted` reduction and the aggregate derivation are pure functions applied by the application; the Mailgun adapter and the secret store are infrastructure adapters invoked from the claimed attempt.
MTX-039.repository: `NotificationRepository`, `NotificationRecipientRepository`, `DeliveryRepository`, `DeliveryAttemptRepository`, `DeliveryReconciliationRepository`, `NotificationEscalationRepository`, `NotificationReplayAcknowledgementRepository`, `NotificationPolicyRepository`, `OutboxMessageRepository`; `IntegrationRepository` and `CredentialRepository` read-and-validate only at the checkpoint; `SupportSessionRepository` read-only; `AccountRepository` and the identity service's current verified delivery address, read-only at each reauthorization.
MTX-039.persistence_model: Canonical `notifications`, `notification_recipients`, `deliveries`, `delivery_attempts`, `delivery_reconciliations`, `notification_escalations`, `notification_replay_acknowledgements` and `outbox_messages` per schemas/POSTGRESQL_SCHEMA.md. `notifications` carries `state CHECK ('pending','uncertain','sent','partial','failed','suppressed')` and unique `(event_id, policy_version, template_version, generation)`. `deliveries` carries `state CHECK ('pending','attempting','accepted','delivered','retry_scheduled','acceptance_unknown','terminal_failed','suppressed')` and unique `(notification_id, recipient_id, channel, replay_generation)`, with Integration/Credential versions always NULL for in-app and nullable for email until individually resolved by an attempt. `delivery_attempts` carries `dispatch_checkpoint CHECK ('prepared','submission_started','recorded')` whose order permits `prepared -> recorded` only for a proven no-submission outcome and otherwise only `prepared -> submission_started -> recorded`. `credentials` carries the frozen `state CHECK ('pending','active','rotating','revoked','expired')` and conceptual pending-material pointer with no secret plaintext and no rotation-token column: the frozen states preserve the conceptual model, but WITHHELD under OD-023 no baseline DDL function or granted path may set pending material, enter `rotating`, or accept replacement material while `UPSTREAM-V1-CREDENTIAL-ROTATION-TOKEN-009` is unresolved. F1 records never contain provider secret bytes, decrypted material, or a value from which the secret can be recovered; secret bytes exist in process memory only for the provider attempt and are zeroized immediately after use.
MTX-039.migration: Not applicable - the canonical schema owns the product tables and this row adds no schema object of its own. WITHHELD under OD-023 and MUST NOT be migrated: any rotation-token column on `credentials`, any DDL function or grant that sets pending material or enters `rotating`, and any `credential_rotation_retry` scheduled-action branch, row or grant. Volume I's `integration-interim-v1` names a `rotation token` field on the Credential while schemas/POSTGRESQL_SCHEMA.md states no rotation-token column; OD-023's own Data Implications records that contradiction and requires the two to be reconciled on correction, so this row adds neither and awaits the controlled change.
MTX-039.transaction_boundary: Event consumption: one transaction creating the Notification, its recipient snapshot and every Delivery, after resolving the union at consumption time. Attempt claim: one transaction atomically claiming the unique `(delivery_id, replay_generation, attempt_number, request_digest)`, persisting the application deduplication and correlation evidence, the required logical adapter-policy identity `mailgun-email-v1`, the executing adapter code version and `dispatch_checkpoint=prepared` - this commits BEFORE Integration/Credential validation and before any provider call. Prepared-stage validation runs inside the claimed attempt and fills the resolved identifiers monotonically; `submission_started` requires the complete valid set and is advanced in its own durable commit before any network write. No external call sits inside a database transaction: the Mailgun submission and the reconciliation query are outside every transaction and only their recorded outcomes commit. Policy activation: one transaction that atomically assigns commit-time effectiveness, activates and supersedes under the Policy Artifact contract. Replay: one transaction creating the linked generation and its acknowledgement record, leaving every source record immutable.
MTX-039.concurrency: The attempt claim is the concurrency control for submission: while the checkpoint is `prepared`, exactly one serialized executor may validate Integration/Credential state, record a proven no-submission outcome, or durably advance to `submission_started` and perform that attempt's first provider submission. Owner or process loss while still `prepared` permits another executor to resume that same not-yet-submitted attempt, which is why resume is safe - nothing has reached the network. At or after `submission_started`, no executor may submit that attempt again, and a crash or incomplete result after that checkpoint is treated as possible provider acceptance rather than as a retry opportunity. Duplicate event consumption, job redelivery, command replay and concurrency reuse that attempt identity rather than create another claim. The outbox route holds a 30-second claim lease. The provider concurrency gate is a separate 4-slot lease acquired immediately before `submission_started` for send or `request_started_at` for reconciliation, with send contenders in exact FIFO `(due_at, delivery_id, attempt_number)` order and a 15-second lease with a five-second heartbeat that stops at the outbound-request checkpoint. A RetryScheduled transition caused by a prior-attempt event atomically cancels its timer, so an authenticated late event and a due retry cannot both fire.
MTX-039.idempotency: Notification creation is idempotent by unique `(event_id, policy_version, template_version, generation)` - the same event consumed twice yields the same Notification rather than a second one. Delivery creation is idempotent by unique `(notification_id, recipient_id, channel, replay_generation)`. Attempt submission is idempotent at the APPLICATION level only, by the atomic claim of `(delivery_id, replay_generation, attempt_number, request_digest)` plus the `submission_started` checkpoint: one claim receives exactly one first submission and no executor re-enters it after `submission_started`. This is explicitly NOT provider-side idempotency. Mailgun supplies none, so the application deduplication key and the Mailgun user-variable correlation token are evidence lookup and local deduplication mechanisms only and cannot guarantee one external delivery; external delivery may be zero, one, or more than one and no exactly-once claim is permitted. Duplicate tolerance is instead carried by the product action: the template retains one logical action reference whose invitation, expiry, authorization, command replay and underlying product-transition rules remain independently idempotent, so a duplicate email duplicates no authority and no product action. Provider event IDs are deduplicated: for one provider event ID only the first authenticated normalized content applies, later byte-equivalent duplicates are ignored, and different normalized content under that ID makes the reconciliation set `ambiguous`.
MTX-039.background_job: `event_consume` executes `notification_route_v1` and claims its `outbox_messages` route row; there is no separate `notification_route` work type. `delivery_execute` claims its `delivery_attempts` row. `delivery_reconcile` claims its `delivery_reconciliations` row. `provider_event_consume` claims a `work_executions` row for authenticated Mailgun event ingress. WITHHELD under OD-023: no `credential_rotation_retry` scheduled action exists, and no branch, row or grant for it may be added while `UPSTREAM-V1-CREDENTIAL-ROTATION-TOKEN-009` is unresolved.
MTX-039.queue: The `delivery` queue carries the outbox route, per the `outbox_messages` fixed `queue_name text CHECK (queue_name='delivery')`. Queue identity and worker topology are owned by BACKGROUND_PROCESSING.md; this row does not rename them.
MTX-039.retry_policy: Only definitive nonacceptance retries, and it retries on a fixed schedule: the initial attempt plus exactly three retries at 1, 5 and 30 minutes after completion of the preceding failed attempt, exhausting at four definitively nonaccepted attempts. Definitive nonacceptance is exhaustively three things: a complete synchronous `429`; Integration initialization dependency or timeout exhaustion after its one-second internal retry; and a transport result that proves no network submission began. `Retry-After` replaces a `429` retry's delay only when its raw value is an unsigned base-10 HTTP delta-seconds integer from `60` through `1800` inclusive, and the delay is then exactly that many elapsed seconds; HTTP-date, signed, fractional, whitespace-containing, malformed and out-of-range values are ignored. Every implicit transport and client retry inside the Mailgun adapter is disabled, so the adapter performs exactly one network submission operation per attempt. `integration-interim-v1` initialization has its own bounded retry - exactly one retry one second later, only for `adapter_initialization_timeout` or `adapter_dependency_unavailable`, under the same attempt generation - and that retry completes INSIDE the claimed attempt and never schedules a second Delivery timer; WF-014 remains the sole owner of Delivery retry timing. Uncertainty always wins over a retry classification: any result for which acceptance cannot be disproved is `acceptance_unknown` and receives no automatic resend at all.
MTX-039.terminal_failure: `terminal_failed` and `suppressed` are absorbing. Terminal on the prepared stage: invalid or missing policy or configuration, a disconnected or retired Integration, or an unavailable, invalid, revoked or expired Credential completes the already-claimed attempt as `terminal_failed` with the exact `integration-interim-v1` reason and makes no Mailgun call. No other prepared-stage failure is retryable. Terminal before any attempt claim: an email Delivery with no current verified delivery address transitions directly to `terminal_failed` with `recipient_address_unavailable`, makes no Mailgun call and claims no attempt. Terminal on the provider result: a complete `400`, `401`, `403`, `404` or other non-`408`/non-`429` `4xx`. Terminal on exhaustion: four definitively nonaccepted attempts give `terminal_failed / provider_retry_exhausted`. Terminal on authenticated evidence: `failed` with permanent severity, `rejected`, `bounced`, `complained` or `unsubscribed`, which has precedence and can change retry-scheduled, acceptance-unknown, accepted or delivered to terminal-failed exactly once. Absence of evidence never proves nonacceptance or terminal failure, and `acceptance_unknown` has no age-based inference: it is neither success nor terminal failure and is never converted to either without exact authenticated provider evidence.
MTX-039.reconciliation: On entering `acceptance_unknown`, read-only reconciliation starts immediately and repeats at exactly 1, 5 and 30 minutes later, giving sequences 0, 1, 2 and 3. It consumes authenticated Mailgun webhooks and events and queries provider event history by the exact correlation token, recipient and replay generation, and it never submits a message. Before state reduction every token-matched record MUST carry the same exact recipient and replay generation and MUST bind unambiguously to this Delivery; a missing or conflicting tuple, one token bound to another recipient, generation or Delivery, or one provider event ID with different normalized content is exactly `ambiguous`. Otherwise one or more exact decisive events reduce by the fixed precedence `terminal_failed > delivered > accepted`, apply that state, and emit one `NotificationDeliveryReconciled` with the contributing event IDs and the selected precedence. The four nonresolving outcomes are exact: zero decisive exact events is `none`, provider query timeout or dependency failure is `dependency_error`, failed event or query authentication is `authentication_failed`, and the tuple violation above is `ambiguous`; each retains `acceptance_unknown`, records the exact result and sends nothing. After the final scheduled query, later exact authenticated provider evidence remains authoritative. A temporary Mailgun delivery failure maps to `accepted`, because Mailgun owns that message's provider-side retry and F1 MUST NOT resend it. Unknown authenticated event types are retained as `provider_event_ignored` and change no state.
MTX-039.domain_events: The seventeen WF-014 events: `NotificationPolicyActivated`, `NotificationCreated`, `NotificationDeliveryAttempted`, `NotificationDeliveryAccepted`, `NotificationDelivered`, `NotificationRetryScheduled`, `NotificationDeliveryAcceptanceUnknown`, `NotificationDeliveryReconciled`, `NotificationDeliverySuppressed`, `NotificationDeliveryFailed`, `NotificationUncertain`, `NotificationSent`, `NotificationPartial`, `NotificationFailed`, `NotificationSuppressed`, `NotificationEscalated`, `NotificationReplayRequested`. Plus the applicable `integration-interim-v1` Integration/Credential events reachable from the checkpoint: `IntegrationProposed`, `IntegrationConnected`, `IntegrationDegraded`, `IntegrationDisconnected`, `IntegrationRetired`, `CredentialProvisioned`, `CredentialActivated`, `CredentialRevoked`, `CredentialExpired`. `NotificationDeliveryAttempted` is emitted only from the terminal `recorded` checkpoint and its physical event field is exactly `recorded`, never an invented `provider_responded` checkpoint. WITHHELD under OD-023: `CredentialRotationStarted` and `CredentialRotated` are canonical Volume I names but no emission, outbox row or Notification route for either exists while the rotation limb is withheld.
MTX-039.event_payload: The canonical envelope with the real `organization_id` and the routed event's Project and lineage values, plus the Notification, Delivery, recipient, channel, replay generation and attempt identity; the policy, template, adapter, Integration, Credential and material versions; the dispatch checkpoint; the reason code; the aggregate outcome; and the provider message and event IDs when known. Prohibited from every payload: raw Evidence payloads, secrets, verification tokens, provider credentials, unrestricted internal errors, message bodies, the correlation-token plaintext and any value from which the secret can be recovered. Reconciliation events additionally carry the contributing event IDs and the selected precedence.
MTX-039.event_producer: `Workflows::Wf014` is the sole producer of all seventeen notification events. The Integration and Credential events are produced by the integration and credential lifecycle services under `integration-interim-v1` and are consumed here rather than produced here. Authenticated Mailgun webhook ingress, provider event IDs, provider status text, transport certainty, `delivery` queue depth, the provider concurrency gate, worker leases, adapter timing and end-to-end latency are technical telemetry and MUST NOT be emitted as domain events.
MTX-039.event_consumers: The outbox route consumer is exactly `notification_route_v1`, which is the required consumer this workflow executes; the event transaction creates that route only when the exact event type and major are active in the effective Notification Policy and complete `notification_context_v1` is present, and otherwise creates no row. WF-014 itself names no downstream consumer of its own seventeen events. The inbox read surface consumes Notification state under `notification.inbox.read`.
MTX-039.serializer: Not applicable - no transport exposure is defined by Volume I; see route.
MTX-039.authorization_entry_point: The application command or the event-consumption handler, before mutation, and AGAIN before every single attempt. Reauthorization per attempt is mandatory and is not an optimisation: before each attempt the platform re-evaluates the route permission, Organization and resource scope, Account status and current verified delivery address, and later loss of authorization becomes `suppressed`, not sent. An authorization decision made at event consumption is never trusted at attempt time. For the direct Invitation route the equivalent per-attempt recheck is that the Invitation remains active, the target digest is unchanged and server time is strictly before expiry. Replay reaches its entry point only through an active support session; the SecurityOperator role alone grants nothing.
MTX-039.permission_checks: Route Required Permissions, each verified present in the Permission Baseline and applied at event consumption and again at every attempt: `invitation.create` for Invitation lifecycle notices to Accounts; `source.scope.propose` for `SourceVerified`; `source.verify` for `SourceVerificationExpired`; `history.read` for `CrawlCompleted` with partial coverage, `CrawlFailed` and `CrawlLimitReached`; `score.summary.read` for `ScoreSnapshotPromoted` with partial status and `ScoreCalculationUnavailable`; `issue.read` for `IssueAdjudicated` and `IssueDisputeWithdrawn`; `issue.adjudicate` for `IssueAdjudicationOverdue`, `IssueAdjudicationReminder` and `IssueAdjudicationCritical`; `entitlement.notice.read` for `EntitlementWarningIssued` and `EntitlementViolationDetected`; `export.retrieve` for `ExportAvailable` and every transition to `ExportFailed`; `security.notice.read` for `SecurityIncidentCustomerActionRequired`. The `InvitationActivated` route uses the matching invitation-bound email binding rather than a permission, and a same-Organization Account when one already exists. Management: `policy.notification.manage`, allow for an OrganizationAdmin for optional informational routes, templates and preferences only, and for a SecurityOperator for security templates, support-queue roster and critical selectors only; it grants neither the other's scope. `notification.replay` is deny for every role except SecurityOperator support-session only. `notification.inbox.read` is allow for own inbox for every human role and deny for service identities. The Notification service identity may invoke only the exact platform-managed integration checkpoint and holds no policy, replay or lifecycle authority. WITHHELD under OD-023: no `credential.rotation_token.issue` permission exists and every mint request is denied as an undefined permission under the Permission Baseline; `credential.rotate` remains a canonical baseline token (SecurityOperator protected explicit grant plus Support Session) but is unreachable because the mandatory fresh rotation token has no defined issuer, format, lifetime, consumption point, binding or transport.
MTX-039.tenant_boundary: Every Notification belongs to the event Organization and every selector component resolves only active Accounts within that Organization and resource scope. The stored recipient snapshot is immutable, so a later roster or authorization change affects reauthorization and suppression but never adds a recipient. Data classification is bounded by the template and recipient ceiling: a classification above that ceiling fails consumption as `notification_event_invalid` rather than delivering. The Mailgun webhook context derives Organization, Integration, Delivery and attempt exclusively from an authenticated restricted locator and trusts no caller-supplied scope, so a provider event cannot name its own tenant. A support session for one Organization authorizes replay in no other.
MTX-039.error_contract: Consumption: a missing trigger-specific field, inconsistent Organization or resource, unknown major schema, or classification above the template or recipient ceiling is `notification_event_invalid`, creates no Notification and no Delivery, and creates one operational escalation within five minutes. Recipient resolution: an empty final authorized union for a mandatory route makes the Notification `failed` with `no_authorized_recipient`, creates no Delivery and creates exactly one operational escalation within 5 minutes, which exists even if no human is then assigned. Pre-attempt: `recipient_address_unavailable` with no Mailgun call and no attempt claim; `informational_email_opt_out` as `suppressed`, which the direct Invitation email may never use. Prepared stage, terminal with the exact `integration-interim-v1` reason: `integration_policy_unavailable`, `credential_unavailable`, `adapter_configuration_invalid`, `operator_disconnected`, `policy_retired`, `credential_material_invalid`, `credential_revoked`, `credential_expired`. Prepared stage, definitively nonaccepted: `adapter_initialization_timeout` and `adapter_dependency_unavailable` after the one-second internal retry, plus a proven no-network-submission transport result. Provider: `429` is definitive nonacceptance; non-`408`/non-`429` `4xx` is terminal; four definitively nonaccepted attempts give `provider_retry_exhausted`. Uncertainty: `provider_acceptance_unknown` classifies as `F1-DEPENDENCY-503`, severity `error`, `retryable=false` for automatic dispatch, recovery `await_provider_reconciliation_or_submit_acknowledged_replay`, and MUST NOT be converted to success, terminal failure, timeout retry or rate-limit retry. Replay: `F1-DOMAIN-409 / duplicate_delivery_risk_unacknowledged`, severity `warning`, `retryable=false`, recovery `acknowledge_duplicate_delivery_risk_and_submit_new_replay_command`, changing nothing and changing no replay generation; `F1-DOMAIN-409 / notification_replay_ineligible` for an unknown mode, wrong source state or source/target mismatch, changing nothing. Authorization denial returns `F1-AUTH-403`, emits one authorization audit event, and performs no state change and no provider call. Integration/Credential command classification: `F1-DOMAIN-409` for stale state and replay conflict, `F1-DATA-409` for invalid policy, configuration or material, `F1-AUTH-403` for missing authority, `F1-DEPENDENCY-503` for named dependency failure, `F1-TIMEOUT-504` for named deadline failure. A provider-visible duplicate after acknowledged replay or provider behaviour is not an error when the local attempt claim and the underlying product action remain unique.
MTX-039.audit_record: Per WF-014 Audit and Observability: the triggering event; recipient-resolution and authorization decisions; redacted field codes; channel; Delivery generation and attempt; the local attempt claim, deduplication and request digests; the `prepared` and `submission_started` checkpoints; Integration, Credential, material and policy versions; the initialization generation, deadline and result; the exact retry and reconciliation scheduled AND actual times; provider timeout and response certainty; provider and adapter versions; the provider message and event ID when known; the provider-status and reconciliation mapping; uncertainty age; reason code; aggregate outcome; escalation ID; the administrative replay acknowledgment; and end-to-end latency. Never recorded: secret material, message bodies, or the raw correlation token. The escalation and replay acknowledgement are themselves immutable decision records carrying `decision_type`, `decision_value`, `decision_status`, the exact nonempty sorted-unique governing `definition_versions`, `input_sha256` and `output_sha256`; the replay row additionally carries the nonblank human rationale, which remains Audit Evidence and is never copied into the machine or Event reason.
MTX-039.observability: Per CAP-021 Observability Requirements: Integration and Credential versions, local deduplication hits, dispatch checkpoints, definitive retries, the acceptance-unknown count AND age, reconciliation outcomes, acknowledged replays, and provider and aggregate success, failure and uncertainty telemetry, never secret material. Uncertainty age is the load-bearing signal here precisely because `acceptance_unknown` has no age-based inference in the product: age is observable and escalatable but never resolves the state. Escalation latency is directly observable against the 5-minute bound. Queue depth, the provider concurrency gate, worker leases and adapter timing are technical telemetry and are asserted absent from the domain event stream.
MTX-039.retention: Notification, Delivery, DeliveryAttempt and reconciliation records fall in the `product_history` retention class at 7 years, computed as 7 elapsed years after record creation or terminal transition, whichever is later, with irreversible destruction after reference-integrity proof. The window is owned by 015 DATA_LIFECYCLE.md; this row states none of its own. Secret material is never persisted at all, so it has no retention: secret bytes exist in process memory only for the provider attempt and are zeroized immediately after use.

TYP-DATA: a matched reduction emits one `NotificationDeliveryReconciled` carrying the contributing event IDs and the selected precedence. TYP-OBS: every terminally failed required Delivery and every Delivery entering `acceptance_unknown` creates exactly ONE escalation within 5 minutes in the SecurityOperator support queue carrying the Notification, recipient, channel, reason, attempts, uncertainty status when applicable and correlation ID. MTX-085.interface_type: Delivery authority, execution and replay rule enforced across the WF-014 dispatch path. PRULE-034 governs CAP-001, CAP-021 and CAP-025 and applies to WF-013 and WF-014. This row owns its CAP-021/WF-014 limb; the WF-013 Invitation and Role limb is owned by S-01 and S-23 and invokes this contract's delivery path rather than reimplementing it. Its owner is Chief Security. It has no decision dependency of its own beyond those the register cites.
MTX-085.route: Not applicable - PRULE-034 is a rule, not an interface.
MTX-085.request_schema: Not applicable - the rule constrains the MTX-039 schema rather than defining one.
MTX-085.command: Enforced within `ConsumeNotificationEvent`, `ExecuteDeliveryAttempt`, `ReconcileDelivery`, `ConsumeProviderEvent` and `RequestNotificationReplay`. This row adds no command.
MTX-085.command_input: Not applicable - constrains the MTX-039 input.
MTX-085.command_output: Not applicable - constrains the MTX-039 output.
MTX-085.actor: As MTX-039 per command. The rule is actor-scoped in one specific respect it states itself: administrative replay of an uncertain Delivery requires explicit duplicate-risk acknowledgment from the replaying SecurityOperator, so the acknowledgment is an actor obligation rather than a system default.
MTX-085.organization_scope: The event Organization; selectors resolve Accounts within that Organization and resource scope only.
MTX-085.aggregate: Notification and Delivery, with Integration and Credential read and validated at the checkpoint.
MTX-085.aggregate_boundary: The rule's ordering clause is what fixes the boundary: 'claim one durable attempt before Integration/Credential validation'. The claim therefore commits on the Delivery root strictly before any Integration or Credential read, which is why a prepared-stage failure can be recorded against a real attempt rather than vanishing.
MTX-085.value_objects: DispatchCheckpoint, RequestDigest, ApplicationDeduplicationKeyDigest, ProviderCorrelationTokenDigest, ReplayMode, ReplayGeneration, DeliveryState, ReasonCode.
MTX-085.domain_service: Not applicable - enforced in the application commands and the adapter.
MTX-085.persistence_model: Not applicable - PRULE-034 introduces no persistent record of its own; it constrains the records MTX-039 writes. Its one persistence-visible demand is that the attempt claim be durable before validation, which the `delivery_attempts` `prepared` checkpoint carries.
MTX-085.migration: Not applicable - no schema object is added by this row. WITHHELD under OD-023: no rotation-token column, rotation DDL function or grant may be migrated.
MTX-085.transaction_boundary: The rule's own ordering: the durable attempt claim commits, THEN Integration and Credential validation runs inside that claimed attempt, THEN `submission_started` commits before any network write. The rule forbids collapsing these into one commit, because a claim that is not durable before validation cannot prove which attempt a prepared-stage failure belongs to.
MTX-085.concurrency: One claimed attempt receives exactly one first submission and no attempt is resubmitted at or after `submission_started`. This is the rule's exact assertion in AC-PRULE-034 and is what makes at-least-once application processing safe without provider idempotency.
MTX-085.idempotency: Application-level only, and the rule says so in both directions. It REQUIRES: at-least-once application attempt processing; one durable claim before validation; local deduplication such that duplicate consumption, redelivery, replay and concurrency reuse the attempt identity; and duplicate-tolerant retained action references so a duplicate email duplicates no authority or product action. It PROHIBITS: claiming provider exactly-once delivery, and treating permitted provider-visible duplicates as a defect. Mailgun supplies no provider-side idempotency and this contract asserts none.
MTX-085.background_job: Not applicable - the rule constrains the commands and workers, not a job of its own.
MTX-085.queue: Not applicable - no queue of its own.
MTX-085.retry_policy: Not applicable - PRULE-034 defines no retry schedule of its own; it constrains which outcomes may retry. Its constraint is exact and exhaustive: retry only exhausted retryable initialization, proven no-network-submission, or definitive provider nonacceptance; disable implicit client and transport retry; suppress automatic resend while acceptance is unknown. The 1-, 5- and 30-minute schedule and the four-attempt bound belong to `notification-policy-v1` and are contracted in MTX-039.
MTX-085.terminal_failure: The rule requires nonretryable prepared-stage failures to terminalize rather than linger, and forbids a false terminal-failure claim. Absence of provider evidence is therefore never terminal: `acceptance_unknown` is the honest outcome and MUST NOT be converted to success or terminal failure.
MTX-085.reconciliation: Read-only exact-token reconciliation is mandatory under the rule and never sends. The uncertain aggregate, the escalation and the user-visible status must all be exposed rather than hidden, which is the rule's transparency limb.
MTX-085.domain_events: Not applicable - PRULE-034 emits no event of its own; it constrains the seventeen WF-014 events and gates `NotificationReplayRequested` behind its acknowledgment requirement.
MTX-085.event_payload: Not applicable - no event of its own. The rule does bound every payload: no sensitive payload or credential leakage.
MTX-085.event_producer: Not applicable - no event of its own.
MTX-085.event_consumers: Not applicable - no event of its own.
MTX-085.authorization_entry_point: Each command before mutation, and again before EVERY attempt - the rule's words are 'reauthorize/redact every attempt', so the per-attempt entry point is mandatory rather than a defensive extra.
MTX-085.permission_checks: The route's Required Permission per baseline route, re-evaluated at every attempt: `invitation.create`, `source.scope.propose`, `source.verify`, `history.read`, `score.summary.read`, `issue.read`, `issue.adjudicate`, `entitlement.notice.read`, `export.retrieve`, `security.notice.read`, plus the invitation binding for the direct Invitation route. `policy.notification.manage` for policy changes within each role's exact scope; `notification.replay` in an active support session for replay; `notification.inbox.read` for own-inbox reads. The rule adds no permission of its own. WITHHELD under OD-023: no `credential.rotation_token.issue` permission exists and every mint request is denied as an undefined permission under the Permission Baseline; `credential.rotate` is a canonical baseline token that remains unreachable while the rotation token contract is withheld.
MTX-085.tenant_boundary: The rule binds delivery to the platform-managed Integration and Credential of the event Organization: 'use only a valid platform-managed Integration/Credential'. There is no customer connector catalogue, no arbitrary endpoint entry and no customer credential-entry journey, so no tenant can point delivery at a provider or credential of its own choosing.
MTX-085.error_contract: As MTX-039. The rule's own error surface is exactly three envelopes fixed by 017 ERROR_MODEL.md: `provider_acceptance_unknown` as `F1-DEPENDENCY-503`, severity `error`, `retryable=false` for automatic dispatch, recovery `await_provider_reconciliation_or_submit_acknowledged_replay`, never converted to success, terminal failure, timeout retry or rate-limit retry; `duplicate_delivery_risk_unacknowledged` as `F1-DOMAIN-409`, severity `warning`, `retryable=false`, recovery `acknowledge_duplicate_delivery_risk_and_submit_new_replay_command`, changing no replay generation; and `notification_replay_ineligible` on the standard `F1-DOMAIN-409` envelope. `provider_retry_exhausted` applies only after four definitively nonaccepted attempts. A provider-visible duplicate after acknowledged replay or provider behavior is not an error when the local attempt claim and the underlying product action remain unique.
MTX-085.audit_record: As MTX-039. PRULE-034's fixture list names the record classes it requires: Invitation target, Integration/Credential, routing/address, local deduplication, prepared-stage outcome, transport retry disablement, response-loss/uncertainty, reconciliation, retry timing, provider-event precedence, aggregate, user status, duplicate-tolerant action, replay-mode/scope/acknowledgment, audit, and escalation.
MTX-085.observability: As MTX-039 - uncertainty must be exposed rather than smoothed over. The rule requires the uncertain aggregate, the escalation and the user-visible status to be exposed, so an unknown Delivery is visible to the operator and to the recipient's own status view, never silently retried and never silently failed.
MTX-085.retention: Not applicable - PRULE-034 defines no retention obligation of its own; the records it constrains fall in the `product_history` class owned by 015 DATA_LIFECYCLE.md.
MTX-085.test_contracts: TYP-SEC: baseline Notifications route through in-app AND Mailgun email Deliveries - no third channel and no delayed channel exists. TYP-DATA: the direct intended-recipient Invitation exception applies exactly once and every other route uses Account permission selectors. TYP-SEC: only a valid platform-managed Integration and Credential is used; no customer connector catalogue, arbitrary endpoint entry or customer credential-entry journey exists. TYP-SEC: every attempt is reauthorized and redacted - authorization present at consumption and absent at attempt time yields `suppressed` and no provider call. TYP-DATA: email execution uses at-least-once APPLICATION attempt processing, asserted distinct from external delivery counts. TYP-DATA: one durable attempt is claimed BEFORE Integration and Credential validation - no Credential read occurs without a durable `prepared` row. TYP-DATA: nonretryable prepared-stage failures terminalize; they neither retry nor linger. TYP-DATA: retry admits exactly three classes and no fourth - exhausted retryable initialization, proven no-network-submission, and definitive provider nonacceptance. TYP-INT: implicit client and transport retry is disabled, asserted at the transport layer. TYP-DATA: `acceptance_unknown` applies whenever provider acceptance cannot be disproved, and automatic resend is suppressed while unknown. TYP-DATA: reconciliation is read-only and exact-token and never submits a message. TYP-OBS: the uncertain aggregate, the escalation and the user-visible status are all exposed. TYP-DATA: action references are duplicate-tolerant - the same logical action reference used twice produces one product transition. TYP-SEC: administrative replay of an UNCERTAIN Delivery requires explicit duplicate-risk acknowledgment; without it `F1-DOMAIN-409 / duplicate_delivery_risk_unacknowledged` changes nothing and changes no replay generation. TYP-SEC: `delivery_replay` targets ONLY the same logical recipient and channel - a fixture asserting any other prior or current recipient, or the in-app channel, fails. TYP-DATA: only `empty_recipient_replay` may resolve a complete current selector union, and only for a Notification failed with `no_authorized_recipient`. TYP-SEC: NO EXACTLY-ONCE CLAIM is made anywhere - no code path, event, status, audit field, schema constraint or user-visible string asserts provider exactly-once delivery. TYP-DATA: permitted provider-visible duplicates are NOT treated as a defect; the fixture asserts the platform reports no failure. TYP-INT: one prepared claim receives exactly one first submission and no attempt is resubmitted after `submission_started`, asserted under concurrency and under job redelivery. TYP-SEC: no false failure and no false success - absence of provider evidence yields neither. TYP-DATA: a permitted duplicate external email causes no duplicate authority and no duplicate product action. TYP-SEC: `SEC-REQ-013` least privilege holds across the route permission set - holding one route's Required Permission delivers no other route's Notification. TYP-OBS: `OBS-REQ-019` telemetry is present for every delivery outcome class and carries no secret material. TYP-DATA: `ERR-REQ-004` and `ERR-REQ-018` envelopes are exact for `provider_acceptance_unknown`, `duplicate_delivery_risk_unacknowledged` and `notification_replay_ineligible`. TYP-DATA: `SB-REQ-003` and `SB-REQ-009` boundary assertions - every Mailgun call is outbound from a claimed attempt and the webhook ingress carries no product authorization. The complete AC-PRULE-034 fixture set is the AC-CAP-021 and AC-WF-014 set asserted in MTX-039; AC-PRULE-034 passes exactly when those pass. WITHHELD under OD-023 and asserted ABSENT: any test asserting credential rotation initiation or completion, a rotation token issuer, permission, entropy, wire format, TTL, equality boundary, one-use consumption point or binding tuple, a `credential.rotation_token.issue` permission, a reachable `BeginCredentialRotation` or any `CompleteCredentialRotation` entry, a path setting pending material or entering `rotating`, a `CredentialRotationStarted` or `CredentialRotated` emission or route, a `credential_rotation_retry` scheduled action, or a rotation DDL function or grant. The settled delivery behaviour above is contracted in full and is NOT blocked; only the rotation limb is isolated under `UPSTREAM-V1-CREDENTIAL-ROTATION-TOKEN-009`. NOT CONTRACTED HERE - the WF-013 limb: PRULE-034 spans WF-013 and CAP-001/CAP-025, whose Invitation lifecycle and Role-expiry notification obligations are owned by S-01 and S-23. Note for those owners: OD-026's Ratified Behavior and WORKFLOW_SPECIFICATIONS.md:349 both assert a mandatory `RoleExpiryBlocked` route at severity `critical` requiring `security.notice.read`, but the `notification-policy-v1` baseline route table carries no such row, and no actor may add a mandatory route. That row is not invented here.
